lead: Local election results are due to be gazetted today, starting a 14-day clock for hung councils like eThekwini to form governments. Unemployment rose to 33.7% in the third quarter, with KZN and Durban joblessness also climbing.

items.title: Election results gazetted today; councils must sit within 14 days
items.summary: Cogta Minister Velenkosini Hlabisa said results would be gazetted on Wednesday, after which new councils must convene within two weeks. KZN Premier Thami Ntuli urged parties to keep councillors safe as coalition talks begin.

items.title: eThekwini coalition talks open with MK Party short of a majority
items.summary: The MK Party holds 86 of 223 seats, ahead of the DA on 57, ANC on 37 and IFP on 15. The DA has ruled out working with MK, and analysts expect an ANC-DA-IFP deal, possibly with ActionSA.

items.title: Unemployment edges up to 33.7% in the third quarter
items.summary: Stats SA's labour survey put the official jobless rate at 33.7%, up from 33.6%. The expanded measure, which includes discouraged work-seekers, stood at 46.3%.

items.title: KZN joblessness jumps to 33.3%; eThekwini rises to 22.2%
items.summary: KwaZulu-Natal added 51,000 unemployed people in the quarter. In eThekwini, employment fell by 18,000, mostly informal jobs, though formal jobs are still well up on a year ago.

items.title: Matlala now says he paid Sibiya R500,000, not R50,000
items.summary: At the Madlanga Commission, Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala revised the figure he gave a day earlier, saying the money was for a family wedding and not linked to a R228m SAPS tender. He also disputed parts of his signed statement.

items.title: Mbeki backs Ramaphosa's reported resignation offer as ANC denies it
items.summary: Former president Thabo Mbeki said Ramaphosa would be right to step aside if reports of an offer are true. ANC secretary-general Fikile Mbalula insists the president is going nowhere after the party's 30.76% result.

items.title: Home Affairs opens digital asylum registration platform
items.summary: Minister Leon Schreiber said the first phase lets asylum seekers register their intention to apply for protection online, opening this week. He said it responds to a Constitutional Court ruling in July.

items.title: GO!Durban starts testing buses on Bridge City-Pinetown route
items.summary: Buses are now running without passengers in dedicated lanes on Corridor 3, the city's first IRPTN route, to test timetables, docking and cashless fares. No passenger launch date has been set.

items.title: Qatar reports progress in US-Iran talks after White House meeting
items.summary: After Qatar's prime minister met Trump, Doha said it saw progress but could not say how close a deal is. Trump agreed to hold off on new strikes while keeping the naval blockade in place.

items.title: Russia, Ukraine and US negotiators meet in Abu Dhabi
items.summary: The third round of three-way talks this year focuses on security guarantees and possible territorial swaps, according to a US official. Russia objects to European participation.

items.title: Europe tells Rubio it must have a seat at Ukraine peace talks
items.summary: At a G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris, Germany's foreign minister said there can be no settlement without Europe. It was Rubio's first meeting with allies since Republicans' midterm losses.

items.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles fired at Riyadh
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it downed missiles aimed at Riyadh and the south, blaming Yemen's Houthis, a day after an attack on a key oil pipeline. No casualties were reported.

items.title: Cameroon sets February date for twice-delayed elections
items.summary: President Paul Biya, 93, decreed legislative and local polls for 7 February 2027, after two postponements and a crackdown on protests that followed his 2025 re-election.

items.title: Rand holds near R16.36 to the dollar
items.summary: Reuters reported the rand little changed on Tuesday morning ahead of jobs data, with the 2035 government bond yield easing to 8.25%.

items.title: Factory output down 3.5% year on year in September
items.summary: Stats SA said manufacturing production was flat month on month after a 3% drop in August. October figures are due on 10 December.

items.title: Hot US inflation knocks gold and stocks; Brent at lowest since August
items.summary: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above forecasts, and Fed governor Waller backed a December hike. Gold fell about 2.6% and Brent settled at $91.49 on Iran de-escalation hopes.

items.title: Erasmus defends two-change Bok side for Friday's France Test
items.summary: Wilco Louw starts at tighthead and Cobus Reinach returns to the bench for the Stade de France clash, while Eben Etzebeth misses out. Erasmus said the Italy win was not physically demanding.

items.title: Bafana host Kenya on Friday in AFCON qualifier
items.summary: Pitso Mosimane's 27-man squad faces Benni McCarthy's Kenya at Orlando on 13 November at 18:00, with the return leg in Nairobi on 17 November.

items.title: Proteas' first Test against Bangladesh starts Sunday at the Wanderers
items.summary: Temba Bavuma leads a squad that welcomes back Tony de Zorzi, Zubayr Hamza and Anrich Nortje; Lungi Ngidi is still rehabbing.

items.title: Tatjana Smith to swim for the Netherlands at the 2028 Olympics
items.summary: South Africa's most decorated Olympian, back from retirement, announced she will represent the Netherlands, saying she has always held both identities.

items.title: Stanford AI100 report says the scaling era is running out of road
items.summary: The 12-expert panel argues future AI progress will rely on better algorithms rather than ever-bigger models, and says AI's economic payoff is not yet visible in the data.
